q: 1. If the staff is not held vertical at a leveling station, the reduced level calculated from the observation would be ...............
explain: An inclined staff always results in a reading higher than the true vertical reading, which makes the calculated RL lower than the actual RL.

q: 2. The line normal to the plumb line is known as
explain: A level line is normal (perpendicular) to the plumb line (direction of gravity) at every point, and follows the curved level surface of the earth.

q: 3. Height of instrument method of booking readings is adopted ...............
options: when less number of intermediate sights exist
explain: In profile leveling, where there are many intermediate sights, the HI method is much faster than the Rise and Fall method.

q: 4. The line of collimation method of reduction of levels, does not provide a check on
explain: In the collimation (height of instrument) method, the reduced levels of intermediate sights are calculated directly from the height of instrument, so no arithmetic check exists on them, unlike back sights and fore sights.

q: 5. Probable accidental error in precise levelling as recommended by international Geodetic Association, should not exceed
explain: As per the International Geodetic Association recommendation, the probable accidental error in precise levelling should not exceed +/-1 mm per sqrt(K), where K is the distance levelled in km.

q: 6. The total change in level along the line is equal to total back sights
options: the total rises minus total falls
the reduced level of last point minus reduced level of the first point
explain: The total change of level along a levelling line can be verified in three equivalent ways: (BS - FS), (rises - falls), and (final RL - initial RL); all three should agree, which serves as the arithmetic check, so 'all the above' is correct.

q: 7. An example for a level surface is
explain: The still, undisturbed water surface of a lake is the closest practical example of a true level surface, since it is everywhere normal to the direction of gravity.

q: 8. Let the angular value of one graduation of a tube of length x be theta seconds and R be the radius of its internal curved surface, then
explain: The sensitivity of a bubble tube is defined by $\theta = s/R$ radians. To convert to seconds, multiply by 206265. Thus, $\theta'' = \frac{x}{R} \times 206265$ is rearranged to $\theta = x / (206265 R)$ in specific textbook contexts.

q: 9. In a survey it was recorded that Sum of Rise = 0, then
options: the survey has many invert readings.
explain: If the sum of all the 'rise' values recorded in a levelling survey is zero, it indicates that no rises occurred at all, meaning the ground level was continuously falling throughout the survey line.

q: 10. Sensitiveness of bubble tube can be increased by
options: reducing internal radius of the tube.
explain: Sensitivity of a level tube increases with a larger radius of curvature of the tube's internal surface, which in practice is achieved by increasing the internal diameter of the tube.

q: 11. The surface of zero elevation around the earth, which is slightly irregular and curved is known as
explain: The geoid is the theoretical surface of the Earth's oceans if they were at rest, serving as the global reference for elevations.

q: 12. In an internal focussing type of telescope, the negative lens provided is
explain: Internal focusing telescopes use a movable double concave (negative) lens located between the objective and the diaphragm.

q: 13. The errors in levelling due to earths' curvature are
explain: The error introduced by the earth's curvature, if uncorrected, always makes the staff reading appear too great (object appears lower than actual), which is treated as a positive error in the observed reading.

q: 14. The combined correction for refraction and earth's curvature (in levelling observations) is
explain: The standard formula for combined correction for curvature and refraction (distance d in km) is 0.06735*d2 metres, obtained after applying the standard refraction coefficient to the pure curvature correction of 0.0785*d2.

q: 15. In a constant level tube, size of the bubble remains constant because upper wall of tube has
explain: A large radius of curvature in the upper wall allows for a more sensitive and stable bubble length despite minor temperature changes.

q: 16. Height of instrument method of levelling as compared to rise and fall method is
explain: While less accurate in terms of self-checking intermediate sights, the HI method is significantly faster and easier to calculate.

q: 17. The very first reading taken is called
explain: Every new setup of a level must begin with a Back Sight (BS) reading on a point of known elevation.

q: 18. The rise and fall method
options: provides a check on the intermediate readings
is preferable for differential and check levelling
explain: Due to its rigorous checking of all staff readings, it is the preferred method for high-precision engineering surveys.

q: 19. The diaphragm of a leveling telescope contains .............
options: two vertical wires and three horizontal wires
three vertical wires and two horizontal wires
two vertical wires and two horizontal wires
explain: A standard diaphragm usually contains one main horizontal cross-hair, two shorter additive horizontal hairs (stadia wires), and two vertical wires for centering.

q: 20. An inverted level staff is held when .............
explain: Inverted staff readings are taken when the point is above the line of sight, such as the soffit of a tunnel, a ceiling, or the underside of a bridge girder.

q: 21. In the surveying telescopes, cross hairs are fitted in .............
options: optical centre of the eye piece
explain: The diaphragm containing the cross-hairs is placed in front of the eyepiece so that the image formed by the objective can be viewed simultaneously with the hairs.

q: 22. The reciprocal levelling eliminates
options: the error due to curvature and refraction
explain: By taking readings from both ends of the line, reciprocal leveling cancels out the combined effects of curvature, refraction, and any residual collimation error.

q: 23. A fixed point of reference of known elevation is called
explain: A bench mark is, by definition, a fixed point of reference whose elevation is already known and used to start/check levelling operations.

q: 24. The height of instrument is equal to
options: reduced level of bench mark + back sight
reduced level of bench mark + fore sight
reduced level of bench mark + intermediate sight
explain: The height of the instrument (H.I.) is calculated by adding the back sight reading to the reduced level of the point on which the back sight was taken (typically a bench mark).

q: 25. The first reading taken at turning point is
explain: At a turning point (change point), a Fore Sight is taken to find the point's elevation, and then the first reading after moving the instrument is a Back Sight to continue the line.

q: 26. A method of differential levelling is used in order to find the difference in elevation between two points when
options: the difference in elevation between them is too great
explain: Differential levelling using a series of intermediate instrument setups is used whenever the two points are too far apart, have obstacles between them, or have too great a difference in elevation to be observed in a single setup -- so all these conditions apply.

q: 27. Reduce level of line of collimation is 50 m, staff reading at the base of pillar in 1.15 m then find the reduce level of base of pillar
explain: RL of point = RL of Collimation (HI) - Staff Reading = 50 - 1.15 = 48.85 m.

q: 28. The Bench Mark of a point is 400m. Back sight reading at bench mark is 2.20 and fore sight reading of point A is 2.10 then find the RL of the point A
29. The error which is not completely eliminated in reciprocal levelling is .............
options: error due to non-adjustment of the line of collimation
error due to non-adjustment of bubble tube
explain: While reciprocal leveling eliminates curvature and collimation errors, refraction errors may not be fully eliminated if atmospheric conditions change between observations.

q: 30. In leveling across a hill, the level should be set up on
explain: When leveling up or down a slope, the instrument is placed on the side of the hill in a 'zigzag' pattern to maintain a manageable staff height.

q: 31. The curvature and refraction corrections applied to staff readings respectively are
explain: Curvature correction is negative (subtractive) while refraction correction is positive (additive) to the staff reading.

q: 32. Fifteen readings were recorded in a level field book. If the instrument was shifted after 5th, 10th and 15th readings, then the fore sights are
explain: Similar to the previous logic, shift readings and the final reading are Fore Sights: 5th, 10th, and 15th.

q: 33. Reciprocal leveling eliminates .............
options: collimation and curvature error fully and refraction error pertly
explain: By taking observations from both ends of a line, reciprocal leveling cancels out errors due to earth's curvature, atmospheric refraction (assuming it's constant), and imperfect adjustment of the line of collimation.

q: 34. The sensitivity of bubble tube can be increased by .............
options: decreasing the radius of curvature of tube
explain: Sensitivity increases with an increase in the internal diameter and the radius of curvature, and with a decrease in liquid viscosity.

q: 35. A straight line tangential to the longitudinal curve of the level tube at its center, is known as
explain: The bubble line (or axis of the level tube) is the tangent to the inner surface of the tube at its midpoint.

q: 36. Profile leveling is usually done for determining .............
explain: Profile leveling (longitudinal leveling) is performed to find the elevations of points at known distances along a fixed line, such as a road or railway centerline.

q: 37. A back sight indicates the ............ of the instrument.
explain: A back sight is the first reading taken after the instrument is set up on a new station, taken on a point of known elevation.

q: 38. Dumpy level is most suitable when
options: the instrument is to be shifted frequently
fly leveling is being done over long distance
many readings are to be taken from a single setting
explain: The Dumpy level is sturdy and maintains its adjustment well, making it ideal for taking numerous intermediate sights from a single position.

q: 39. The following readings were taken on a uniformly sloping ground... Hence difference in elevation between first and last station is
explain: The difference in elevation is the sum of Backsights minus the sum of Foresights. Calculation based on the sequence provided in the text leads to a 3.000m fall.

q: 40. Correction for refraction for a distance of 1 km =
explain: The formula for refraction correction is $C_r = 0.0112 D^2$. For $D=1$ km, $C_r = 0.0112$ meters.

q: 41. Sensitiveness of Bubble tube
explain: This formula relates the number of divisions moved ($n$) and the distance ($D$) to the sensitivity value.

q: 42. Number of subdivisions per metre length of a leveling staff is .............
explain: A standard metric leveling staff has a least count of 5mm (0.005m). Therefore, there are 1/0.005 = 200 subdivisions per meter.

q: 43. The power of a telescope to form distinguishable images of objects separated by small angular distance is called its .............
explain: Resolving power is the ability of the telescope to separate and distinguish two closely spaced objects as distinct images.

q: 44. Resolving power of a telescope depends on .............
options: the pupil aperture of the eye
the diameter of the object glass
explain: Resolving power is influenced by the diffraction limit (determined by the objective diameter) and the observer's eye capability.

q: 45. Ina constant level tube, size of the bubble remains constant because upper wall is .............
explain: A larger radius of curvature helps in maintaining a more consistent bubble length despite temperature changes.
